turns.content: In Python, what is the difference between a list and a tuple, and when is each the better choice?

Lists are mutable: elements can be added, removed or replaced in place. Tuples are immutable once created. A tuple is hashable when all of its elements are, so it can serve as a dictionary key or a set member; a list cannot. Lists suit collections whose size or order changes; tuples suit fixed records such as coordinates or multiple return values. Tuples also carry slightly less memory overhead.
